findings.claim: Still open, and partly caused by the cycle-2 fix. The effect classes, the absence of implicit persistence, the `sense record` argv and the order `sense run` → `sense record` → `check --only sensor-integrity` are now correct. The `sense run` argv is not. `devai sense run --preset baseline --repo-root . --as-role engineer --format json` is refused before any sensor runs, so the chain cannot start. In DEVAI 1.5.6, the authority contract for `sense run` is `effect: remote-write` with `consent: { write: true, allow_publish: true }` (release-host.js about lines 12890-12916). The host boundary returns `AUTHORITY_WRITE_CONSENT_REQUIRED` when there is no `--write` (197472). For `remote-write` without `--dry-run` it returns `AUTHORITY_PUBLISH_CONSENT_REQUIRED` when there is no `--publish` (197473). The public manifest adds `--write` and `--publish` to this action (191685-191691). The host strips both flags before dispatch (191500), which is why the handler option list (219138-219140) does not show them. Cycle 2 read only that list when it said `run` has no `--write`. So the sentence 'O `--write` pertence ao verbo `record`, não faz `run` persistir' is wrong about consent, even though it is right that `run` does not persist. The block clause stops an empty check from being approved. But A1-2 (line 52) asks the Owner to approve a chain whose first command fails for certain. It also leaves out an Owner decision the runtime requires: CI must give remote-publish consent (`--publish`) to an action that declares `net:sensor-runtime` and `fs:proofs`.
findings.fix: In line 32 and in A1-2, change the first step to `devai sense run --preset baseline --repo-root . --as-role engineer --write --publish --format json`. Explain that `--write`/`--publish` are consent flags the authority contract requires (write: true, allow_publish: true). They do not persist the reading, because `implicit_persistence` stays false. Keep `sense record --input <arquivo> --repo-root . --as-role engineer --write --format json` (consent write: true, allow_publish: false). In A1-2, ask the Owner to decide explicitly on remote-publish consent for `sense run` in the ephemeral CI job, as a separate item or alongside the `sense record` delegation. Require the clone rehearsal (maestro §1(19)) to show three things: no remote publication or writes under `record/` actually happen, the role is accepted, and `readings_scanned > 0`. Otherwise the gate stays blocked.
